title: Cape Cod Home Rebates 2026: Mass Save Heat Pumps, Weatherization, Solar
desc: Cape Cod home rebates for 2026: Mass Save heat pump rebates up to $8,500, free assessments, weatherization, solar and batteries, with details for oil homes and seasonal properties.
badge: Up to $8,500 for a whole-home heat pump
lead: Barnstable County has about 166,000 homes, but only about 106,000 are occupied year-round. That gap, and the share of homes still on oil, decide which rebates apply on the Cape.
cards_heading: What is open for Cape Cod homes in 2026
cards_intro: Cape Light Compact is one of the Mass Save sponsors listed for the heat pump rebate, so confirm which sponsor serves your town. Each card names the program page we read on October 3, 2026.

cards.title: Whole-home heat pump
cards.note: $2,650 per ton for a whole-home air-source system, up to $8,500, for homes replacing oil, propane or electric resistance heat, or natural gas heat through a gas sponsor. Installed by a Mass Save heat pump installer in 2026.

cards.title: Income-qualified heat pump
cards.note: Enhanced rebates for moderate-income and income-eligible households. This is not the standard amount.

cards.title: Home energy assessment
cards.note: The no-cost assessment unlocks the weatherization offers.

cards.title: Decarbonization consultation
cards.note: A no-cost virtual consultation with a Mass Save Decarbonization Specialist, plus a Heating Comparison Calculator that compares the annual cost of different systems. Useful if you do not know where to start.

cards.title: Insulation and air sealing
cards.note: 75% is the standard offer. 100% generally applies to income-qualified households or certain buildings with one to four units.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Instant rebate when replacing an electric, oil, propane or gas water heater.

cards.title: Solar (SMART)
cards.note: A flat payment per kWh for systems up to 25 kW in National Grid, Eversource and Unitil territory. The state tax credit is 15% of cost, up to $1,000.

cards.title: Battery
cards.note: A 5 kW battery enrolled in ConnectedSolutions earns about that over summer events. The HEAT Loan can finance it at 0%, up to $25,000.

cards.title: Federal credits
cards.note: The 25C and 25D credits do not apply to 2026 installs.

sections: Homes that are not lived in all year

The 2020-2024 American Community Survey counts 166,215 housing units in Barnstable County and 105,777 occupied households, so roughly a third of homes are not occupied year-round. Mass Save's rules for seasonal and vacation properties are not on the program pages we read, so we cannot say how a second home is treated. If that is your situation, ask Mass Save before you plan around a rebate.

About 81% of Cape households own and about 82% live in detached houses. Few homes are in two- to four-unit buildings (about 6%), so the landlord-focused rules matter less here than in an inner-city triple-decker. The usual claimant is a homeowner replacing a system.

The ACS estimates about 61% of occupied Cape homes use utility gas, 19% fuel oil, 13% electricity and about 5% bottled gas. The heat pump rebate is written around what you replace. Oil, propane and electric resistance qualify through the electric sponsor, and gas homes through the gas sponsor. Oil is where the switch tends to save most, because the rebate is paid for replacing it and a heat pump cuts the fuel you buy.

About 56% of Cape homes were built before 1980, a lower share than in inner Boston-area cities like Lynn or Salem, and about 13% were built since 2000. The free assessment will tell you whether air sealing or insulation should come before a heat pump is sized.

Mass Save's electric sponsors include Eversource, National Grid, Unitil and Cape Light Compact. Municipal light plant towns are separate. Which one applies depends on your address, so confirm it first and then ask the installer to fit the paperwork to that sponsor.

Since January 1, 2026 Mass Save has removed heat pumps with a high-warming refrigerant, including R-410A, from its qualified list. If a contractor quotes one, you will not get the rebate. Ask which refrigerant is in the unit before you sign.
claim_heading: How to claim on Cape Cod
claim_steps: If you are not sure where to start, book Mass Save's no-cost virtual consultation with a Decarbonization Specialist or try its Heating Comparison Calculator.
Confirm your electric and gas sponsors with Mass Save.
Book the free home energy assessment.
Ask whether your property type, year-round or seasonal, changes eligibility.
Get quotes from a Mass Save heat pump installer and ask which refrigerant the unit uses.
Keep invoices and model numbers for the rebate paperwork.
faq: Does Cape Cod get Mass Save rebates?
Yes, through the sponsors serving each town. Cape Light Compact is one of the sponsors listed for the heat pump rebate.
We could not confirm how Mass Save treats seasonal homes, so ask Mass Save before planning around a rebate.
How much is the heat pump rebate on Cape Cod?
Up to $8,500 for a whole-home system under the standard offer, and no cost or up to $16,000 for income-qualified households.
Is oil heat common on Cape Cod?
The ACS estimates about 19% of occupied Cape homes heat with fuel oil, and about 61% with utility gas.
Is there a federal tax credit in 2026?
No. The federal home energy credits ended for installs after December 31, 2025.
